data.narrative:
ADASI, a sovereign-funded defense and security company acquired by EDGE Group, operates within a sector comprising 26 peers across public and private markets. The comparable universe includes 2 public entities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private companies, with notable private peers including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The Defense & Security sector contains insufficient narrow-stage comparables—zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-valuation-tier peers meeting the three-datapoint minimum threshold necessary for reliable median extraction. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material measurement error given the heterogeneity in technology maturity, contract exposure, and defense customer concentration across the broader peer set.

Without sufficient stage-matched or tier-matched comparables, triangulation yields no supportable range. Deriving valuation for an acquired sovereign-funded entity additionally presents methodological constraints: acquisition prices often embed strategic premiums, cost-of-capital advantages, or geopolitical considerations unobservable in open-market comparable data. A credible valuation would require either (1) access to transaction documentation, (2) expansion of the comparable set to adjacent sectors, or (3) precedent transactions within the narrower defense-tech acquiree cohort. The current dataset does not support quantitative range estimation.
